tables.name: parked_turns
tables.description: Rosie's team's record of a parked turn: a turn that crashed a third time before its commit is parked for Rosie's team, freeing the inbox for later texts; the person hears once that nothing changed and that Rosie's team will reply within 1 business day (arch 11 line 576, DD). The turn itself, with state parked, parked_at and tries 3, is K-04's turns row; this row holds what the team needs: why it crashed, when the person was told, when the reply is due, and the reply. Shown in the team console (C-194).
tables.source: arch 11 line 576; C-180; C-194; Q-18; NQ-RT-3 (the turns row is written once, as committed or parked); 02-contracts section 7 row K-37 ('Parked turns')

columns.name: turn_id
columns.description: The parked turn (turns.id), whose core row has state parked. One record per parked turn.
columns.source: arch 11 line 576; K-04 v1 turns (state parked, parked_at, tries)

columns.name: error_summary
columns.description: The third crash's error as the runtime caught it, for the team: the error's own text, never a private value from the turn's texts, which stay sealed (traces never carry personal data: K-04 v1 handles.address; arch 10 line 516).
columns.source: arch 11 line 576 ('A third crash before the commit parks the turn for Rosie's team'); C-180; arch 10 line 516

columns.name: person_told_at
columns.description: When the person was told, once, that nothing changed and that Rosie's team will reply within 1 business day. Set once; null until the line has gone. Whether it goes to a stopped number is limit 8's (RULES 7.2), not this row's.
columns.source: arch 11 line 576 ('the person hears once that nothing changed and that Rosie's team will reply within 1 business day (DD)')

columns.name: reply_due_at
columns.description: When the team's reply is due: 1 business day after the turn was parked, as code computes it (README open gaps: the business-day calendar).
columns.source: arch 11 line 576 ('within 1 business day (DD)'); Q-18

columns.name: state
columns.description: open: waiting for the team's reply; replied: a person on Rosie's team has replied to the person.
columns.source: arch 11 line 576 ('Rosie's team will reply'); C-194

columns.name: replied_at
columns.description: When the team replied; set with state replied.
columns.source: arch 11 line 576

columns.name: replied_by_person_id
columns.description: The person on Rosie's team who replied (persons.id; until launch Jay or the CTO, Q-18). Set with state replied.
columns.source: Q-18; C-194; arch 09 line 457 (who)

columns.name: resolution
columns.description: What the team did, in plain words and without private values (RULES 4.5): for example re-ran the turn from its sealed texts, or handled the request by hand. Set with state replied.
columns.source: arch 11 line 576; C-194; RULES 4.5

columns.name: version
columns.description: The row's version: every update raises it by one, and a commit compares and sets it, so a write made from an old read is refused with the rows that changed (limit 4).
columns.source: arch 01 line 85; arch 10 line 506; K-04 v1 rule 2

checks.name: parked_turns_replied_has_who
checks.expression: state <> 'replied' or (replied_by_person_id is not null and resolution is not null)

indexes.name: parked_turns_open_due_idx
indexes.why: The team console's parked turns, the reply due soonest first (C-194; arch 11 line 576).

tables.name: dead_letters
tables.description: The dead-letter queue in the team console: a queued job other than a send that failed its 5 tries. Queues carry retries only: sends follow step 8 and never land here; other jobs get 5 tries, then the dead-letter queue (arch 10 line 540, DD). Effects take their service's outage row instead (arch 10 line 542). One row per job that ran out of tries; the team replays it or closes it.
tables.source: arch 10 line 540 ('other jobs get 5 tries, then a dead-letter queue in the team console (DD)'); arch 02 diagram line 105 ('Team console: paging · gap cases · dead letters'); C-035; C-056; C-194; 02-contracts section 7 row K-37

columns.source: CQ-09 (other ids are opaque strings)

tables.name: gap_cases
tables.description: A gap case: a turn that no choice fit, logged with its state and frontier for the weekly review (arch 01 line 95). Nothing fits: meaning search adds the 3 closest entry steps and the turn's one re-read runs; still nothing: the Sonnet planner; a reply to its question that fits nothing goes to a person. Each such turn is a gap case; the team reviews them weekly, and each miss becomes a test and a fix (arch 03 line 189; HANDOFF 10).
tables.source: arch 01 line 95; arch 03 line 189; arch 06 line 291 (log a gap case); K-02 v1 plannerLogGap, choice; C-194; 02-contracts section 7 row K-37 ('gap cases with their state and frontier')

columns.name: turn_id
columns.description: The turn that nothing fit (turns.id). One gap case per turn: 'Each such turn is a gap case' (arch 03 line 189).
columns.source: arch 01 line 95 ('A turn that no choice fit'); arch 03 line 189

columns.name: business_id
columns.description: The business whose step graph meaning search ran over (businesses.id); null when the turn was about no one business yet.
columns.source: arch 03 line 189 ('meaning search over this business's step graph')

columns.name: outcome
columns.description: What happened to the turn: one of the planner's five verbs as K-02 v1's plannerOutput names them (answer, ask, pass_on, hand_off, log_gap: arch 06 line 291), or to_person, when a reply to the planner's question fit nothing and went to a person (arch 03 line 189; S13-29 rule 54).
columns.source: arch 03 line 189; arch 06 line 291; K-02 v1 plannerOutput; S13-29 rule 54

columns.name: summary_sealed
columns.description: What the person wanted that nothing fit, in plain words: K-02 v1 plannerLogGap.summary for log_gap. Sealed under the key of sealed_for_person_id, since it may carry the person's private details (RULES 4.5: when unsure, treat it as private); unreadable once that key is deleted. Null when the planner gave no summary.
columns.source: K-02 v1 plannerLogGap.summary; arch 09 line 492; arch 01 line 93; RULES 4.5, 4.10

columns.name: sealed_for_person_id
columns.description: The person whose key seals summary_sealed (persons.id): the person who wrote the turn. One person per row, as K-04's event_log.
columns.source: arch 09 line 492; K-04 v1 event_log.sealed_for_person_id

columns.name: open_question_ids
columns.description: Its state, part one: the open questions sent to this handle when the turn ran (open_questions.id; K-02 v1 context openQuestions), so the review sees what was being asked. Empty when none was open.
columns.source: arch 01 line 95 ('logged with its state'); arch 09 line 455 ('Open questions are the memory of every conversation'); K-02 v1 context.openQuestions

columns.name: versions_read

columns.source: arch 01 line 95; K-04 v1 open_questions.versions_read; K-02 v1 fact (table, rowId, version)

tables.name: review_items
tables.description: The team review queue: each thing the sources send to a person on Rosie's team, never to the AI alone, with when it is due. Within 1 business day: a new kind of work drafted from the owner's words (S1-03), control of a business (S1-75), a listing that does not match or is already on Rosie (S1-76), an owner of record's claim (S11-52), bookings over a phone or address limit (S12-28). The same day: harm to a child, an older adult or someone in care (A3-49), a report that the owner or staff harmed someone, and a deadline the law sets that Rosie missed (S11-70). The thing reviewed lives in its own part (a business, a new-work draft, a harm report); this row is the queue entry that points at it.

columns.name: id
columns.description: The review item's id: an opaque string code makes and never parses (CQ-09).
columns.source: CQ-09 (other ids are opaque strings)

columns.name: kind
columns.description: new_work (S1-03: the plug-in draft and each service against the official rules for that work), control (S1-75: Rosie's team checks control when no code came back from the listing's own phone or email), listing_match (S1-76: a listing that does not match, or a business already on Rosie), owner_claim (S11-52: an owner of record claims a business set up by someone who is not one; the team checks the papers), booking_cap (S12-28: one phone or address over the plug-in's daily cap), harm_report (A3-49; S11-70: harm told of, or a report that the owner or staff harmed someone), missed_deadline (S11-70: a deadline the law sets that was missed).

columns.name: business_id
columns.description: The business it is about (businesses.id); null when it is about no one business.
columns.source: S1-75 ('That company stays offline until then'); S1-76; S11-52; S12-28; arch 10 line 546

columns.name: subject_table
columns.description: The table of the row under review, named as K-04's event_log.table_name names a row, for example businesses for control and listing checks. Null while the row's part is not frozen (README open gaps: K-24's new-work draft, K-34's harm report). Set with subject_row_id.
columns.source: K-04 v1 event_log.table_name, row_id; K-02 v1 fact (table, rowId)

columns.name: subject_row_id
columns.description: The primary key of the row under review, as text; no foreign key, since it may be in any part. Set with subject_table.
columns.source: K-04 v1 event_log.row_id

columns.name: turn_id
columns.description: The turn that raised it (turns.id), or null when a job or a page raised it.
columns.source: 02-contracts K-08 ('the turn id, or a job id'); K-04 v1 turns

columns.name: raised_by_person_id
columns.description: Who asked for the review (persons.id): the owner setting up (S1-03, S1-75, S1-76) or the owner of record claiming (S11-52). Null when Rosie raised it: a harm report she was told of (A3-49), the cap flag (S12-28), a missed deadline (S11-70). A harm report never names its reporter here: the report and who made it are kept with the report itself (README open gaps, K-34).
columns.source: S1-03; S1-75; S1-76; S11-52; A3-49 ('Nothing they said reaches the family or the booker'); S12-28; S11-70

columns.name: summary
columns.description: What the team must check, in plain words, without private values: those stay in the row under review, sealed where its part seals them (RULES 4.5, 4.10). For example S12-28's flag: 'One phone tried to book more visits today than the plug-in allows. Nothing was booked.'

columns.name: opened_at
columns.description: When it entered the queue.

columns.name: due_at
columns.description: When the team's answer is due, as code computes it from the kind: within 1 business day for new_work, control, listing_match, owner_claim and booking_cap (S1-03, S1-75, S1-76, S11-52, S12-28); the same day for harm_report and missed_deadline (A3-49 'a person on Rosie's team follows up today'; S11-70 'the same day'). README open gaps: the business-day calendar.
columns.source: S1-03; S1-75; S1-76; S11-52; S12-28 ('within 1 business day'); A3-49 ('today'); S11-70 ('the same day')

columns.name: state
columns.description: open: waiting for the team; waiting: waiting on someone else until wait_until (S11-52: the account owner is told and has 3 business days to send their own papers); done: the team decided.
columns.source: S11-52 ('has 3 business days to send their own papers'; 'Rosie's team decides on both'); C-194

columns.name: wait_until
columns.description: While waiting, when the wait ends: for an owner claim, 3 business days after the account owner was told (S11-52). Null otherwise.

columns.name: decided_at
columns.description: When the team decided; set with state done.
columns.source: S11-52 ('Rosie's team decides'); S1-03 ('Sam hears the result within 1 business day')

columns.name: decided_by_person_id
columns.description: The person on Rosie's team who decided (persons.id; until launch Jay or the CTO, Q-18). Set with state done.
columns.source: Q-18; C-194; arch 09 line 457 (who)

columns.name: outcome
columns.description: The team's decision in plain words, without private values: for example control proven or not, the claim granted or refused, the services checked. Set with state done; what it changes is written to the row under review in its own part.

columns.name: version
columns.description: The row's version: every update raises it by one, and a commit compares and sets it, so a write made from an old read is refused with the rows that changed (limit 4).
columns.source: arch 01 line 85; arch 10 line 506; K-04 v1 rule 2

checks.name: review_items_waiting_has_until
checks.source: S11-52 (3 business days to send their own papers)

checks.name: review_items_done_has_who
checks.expression: state <> 'done' or (decided_by_person_id is not null and outcome is not null)

indexes.why: The team console's review queue, the answer due soonest first (C-194; Q-18).

indexes.name: review_items_subject_idx
indexes.why: A row's reviews, for example whether a business still waits on its control check (S1-75).

indexes.name: review_items_business_idx
indexes.why: One business's reviews, for the team (S1-76, S11-52, S12-28).

rowLevelSecurity.why: Rosie's team's queue across every business (Q-18; C-194). Some items must never reach the business they are about (S11-70: a report that the owner or staff harmed someone comes here, never only to the one named; S12-28: patterns across businesses are seen only by Rosie's team), so the Tool API roles have no grant on it (README rule 2).
